function.name: code_run
function.description: Code executor. Prefer python. Multi-call OK, use script param. Reply code block is executed if no script arg; prefer for single call to avoid escaping. No hardcoding bulk data

script.description: [Mutually exclusive] NEVER use this param when use reply code block.

inline_eval.description: DO NOT USE except explicitly specified.

function.name: file_read
function.description: Read file. Read before modify for latest context and line numbers

keyword.description: [Optional] If provided, returns first match (case-insensitive) with context

function.name: file_read_batch
function.description: Batch read-only preview of up to 12 files in one call. Returns per-file head or keyword-hit context plus total-lines & truncation flag. Use for SOP+TODO+history+candidate scans instead of N sequential file_read calls

paths.description: Up to 12 file paths (relative or absolute). Duplicates auto-deduped

keyword.description: [Optional] If provided, every file returns the first case-insensitive match's surrounding lines instead of the head

function.name: task_closure_check
function.description: Read-only autonomous-task closure verifier. Snapshots whether the current R<n> report file exists, whether history.txt was prepended, how many TODO checkboxes remain, and how many approvals_board / pm_proposals items are still open. Returns a missing-step suggestion list. Does NOT mutate files or status

report_id.description: [Optional] e.g. "R42". If omitted, uses the highest R<n> found under autonomous_reports/

temp_root.description: [Optional] Root containing autonomous_reports/, TODO.txt, approvals_board.md. Defaults to handler cwd

function.name: self_readme
function.description: Generate an AI-Native developer Readme by aggregating temp/cost_ledger.jsonl + git log + temp/activity/ + autonomous reports. Inspired by Readme.skill (study8677/Readme.skill); reproduces the same output from local data without cloning the upstream skill. Returns the rendered markdown

anonymize.description: Replace project/model/author names with `Project A`, `Model B`, etc. for shareable output

write.description: Also write to disk (temp/self_readme.md unless `out` is given)

function.name: file_patch
function.description: Replace unique old_content with new_content. Exact match required (whitespace/indentation). On failure, file_read to recheck

old_content.description: Original text block to replace (must be unique)

new_content.description: New content. Supports {{file:path:startLine:endLine}} to ref file lines, auto-expanded

function.name: file_write
function.description: Create/overwrite/append files. ONLY for HUGE edits. Place <file_content>...</file_content> in reply body BEFORE the file_write call. Supports {{file:path:startLine:endLine}}, auto-expanded

function.name: web_scan
function.description: Get simplified HTML and tab list. Removes hidden/floating/covered elements. Call after switching pages

tabs_only.description: Show tab list only, no HTML

function.name: web_execute_js
function.description: Execute JS. Multi-call OK with different switch_tab_id. No guessing. Act accurately to reduce web_scan calls. Execute JS in ```javascript blocks if no script arg, prefer to avoid escaping

script.description: [Mutually exclusive] JS code or script path. NEVER use this param when use reply code block

no_monitor.description: Skip page change monitoring, saves 2-3s. Only for reads, not for page actions

switch_tab_id.description: [Optional] Tab ID to switch to before executing

function.name: update_working_checkpoint
function.description:
Short-term working notepad, auto-injected each turn to prevent info loss in long tasks. Call during early/mid stages, not at end. When: (1) after reading SOP, store user needs & key constraints (skip for simple 1-2 step tasks); (2) before subtask switch or context flush; (3) after repeated failures, re-read SOP and must store new findings; (4) on new task, update content, clear old progress but keep valid constraints.

Don't call: simple tasks (1-2 steps), task completed (use long-term memory tool)

key_info.description: Replaces current notepad (<200 tokens). Incremental update: review existing, keep valid, add/remove/modify. Store: pitfalls, user requirements, key params/findings, file paths, progress, next steps. Don't store: ephemeral info, obvious context, old task info when user switched tasks. Prefer over-updating over losing key info

related_sop.description: Related SOP names, tips for further re-read

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Interrupt task to ask user when needing decisions, extra info, or facing unresolvable blockers

candidates.description: Optional quick-select choices for the user

function.name: start_long_term_update
function.description: Start distilling long-term memory. Call when discovering info worth remembering (env facts/user prefs/lessons learned). Skip if memory already updated or in autonomous flow. Must call when a task that took 15+ turns is completed

function.name: sop_search
function.description: Search Sophub (fudankw.cn/sophub) for SOPs / shared skills others uploaded. Use this as a first move on unfamiliar tasks — there may already be a verified workflow you can reuse instead of figuring it out from scratch. Returns top results with id, title, score and a short preview.

query.description: Natural-language query (zh or en both fine)

function.name: sop_read
function.description: Fetch the full content of a specific SOP by id (id from sop_search). Use BEFORE applying an SOP so you have the actual steps, not just the preview.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Real-time web search via Grok native live_search (web/x/news) + Tavily REST in parallel. Use when the answer needs current/external info (markets, academic, news, product comparisons, regulations). Workflow: first try sop_search for an internal SOP; if nothing fits, call web_search. For deep multi-hop research, follow memory/web_search_sop.md to spawn a subagent. Always cite urls in your reply. Never silent-fail — even if one source errors, the other side's results are returned with an [error] banner.

depth.description: Tavily depth. Use 'advanced' for Chinese queries or complex/multi-step questions.

function.name: wechat_send
function.description: Send a WeChat message to a contact or group via wxauto (UI automation). Outbound only — no history reads, no listeners. Prerequisites: PC WeChat (Windows) running, logged in, foregroundable; `pip install wxauto`. Tested on WeChat 3.9.x; on 4.x or version mismatch the call returns an error string and you should fall back via `sop_read wechat_ljqctrl_sop`. Side effects are real and irreversible — the user will see the message land. Do not call without explicit user instruction.

to.description: Contact remark / nickname / group name. Must be searchable from the recipient's WeChat address book (the same string you'd type in the search bar).

text.description: Plain-text message body. Newlines are sent literally (no Ctrl+Enter quirk).

files.description: Optional list of absolute local file paths to send as attachments after the text.

function.name: mcp_call
function.description: Single-entry gateway to every configured MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. Use this to access external capabilities the user has installed (filesystem servers, GitHub, databases, custom internal tools, etc.) without GA needing a dedicated tool for each. Three usage patterns: (1) Call with NO arguments to list all configured servers. (2) Call with only `server` set to list the tools that server exposes. (3) Call with `server`, `tool`, and `arguments` to actually invoke a tool. Always discover before invoking — server tool names and schemas are user-controlled and not knowable in advance. Returns plain text suitable for direct reading.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list configured servers.

tool.description: Tool name on that server. Omit to list the server's tools.

arguments.description: Tool arguments — match the server's inputSchema as returned by the discovery list.

function.name: process
function.description: Background-process registry. Use this whenever you spawn a long-running OS process (browser, shell, watcher, headless agent) so it remains visible and killable across turns. Without it the pid scrolls off chat history and you can't reap zombies. Actions: (1) `register` — record a process you've already spawned, with a label you'll use to refer to it later; (2) `list` — show all registered processes with `alive` flags; (3) `kill` — terminate by pid OR label; (4) `cleanup_dead` — drop entries whose pids are no longer alive. Default action is `list`.

label.description: Human-readable handle. Required for `register`. Optional for `kill` (kills all entries with this label).

pid.description: OS pid. Required for `register`. Optional for `kill` (alternative to label).

cmd.description: Original command line, for log clarity.

force.description: On `kill`: escalate to SIGKILL / taskkill /F if the graceful terminate hangs.

function.name: checkpoint
function.description: Persist intermediate state for long tasks so a restart / context-flush doesn't erase progress. Storage is per-task; checkpoints accumulate up to 50 per task (oldest dropped). Actions: (1) `save` — write a new checkpoint, returns its id; (2) `load` — read the latest (or named via `checkpoint_id`); (3) `list` — enumerate without state body; (4) `clear` — delete all checkpoints for the task; (5) `list_tasks` — show every task that has at least one checkpoint. Use 1+ snapshots into multi-step tasks; `state` is whatever JSON you need to resume.

task_id.description: Stable id for the task (e.g. 'refactor-auth-2026-05-04'). Required for save/load/list/clear.

state.description: Arbitrary JSON-serialisable state. Required for save.

checkpoint_id.description: Specific checkpoint id for load. Omit to fetch the most recent.

function.name: vision
function.description: Unified image-understanding tool. Sends an image (path or bytes) to the user's configured vision-capable LLM. Actions: (1) `describe` — free-form description; (2) `ocr` — extract visible text only; (3) `extract` — return JSON matching `schema`. Routes automatically to the first claude-vision or gpt-vision config in mykey. Returns a string for describe/ocr, a dict for extract. On failure returns `'Error: ...'` so you can branch on prefix.

image_path.description: Filesystem path to the image (png/jpg/webp/etc). Required.

prompt.description: Optional override prompt. Defaults sane for each action.

schema.description: Required for `extract` — describe the JSON shape you want back.

function.name: gui_operator
function.description: Desktop GUI operator inspired by UI-TARS. Actions: (1) `observe` captures the current desktop screenshot to temp/gui_runs and returns path/size/scale; (2) `parse` parses UI-TARS-style action text such as click(start_box='[x1,y1,x2,y2]') into coordinates; (3) `act` executes one parsed desktop action; (4) `run` performs a small screenshot -> configured vision/VLM -> action loop. Defaults to dry_run for safety. Real clicks/typing are irreversible and require explicit user intent.

output_path.description: Optional screenshot output path for observe. Defaults to temp/gui_runs/YYYYMMDD/.

include_base64.description: For observe: include screenshot base64 in the result. Usually false; use the returned path with vision instead.

all_screens.description: For observe: capture all monitors when supported. Single-monitor is safer for coordinate actions.

instruction.description: For run: natural-language desktop task given to the vision model.

prediction.description: For parse: raw VLM output containing one or more Action lines.

action_text.description: For parse/act: one action call, e.g. click(start_box='[100,200,120,220]') or hotkey(key='ctrl+l').

screen_width.description: Logical screen width used for coordinate conversion. Required for parse on non-observe data.

screen_height.description: Logical screen height used for coordinate conversion. Required for parse on non-observe data.

scale_factor.description: DPI scale factor from observe; defaults to 1.0.

loop_wait.description: For run: seconds to wait between real actions.

backend.description: For run: vision backend, same values as vision_tools (`auto`, `claude`, `openai`).

dry_run.description: For act: parse and return coordinates without moving mouse/keyboard.

function.name: browser_operator
function.description: Hybrid browser operator. Defaults to DOM/text scan and instructs use of web_execute_js when the page is structured; switches to visual gui_operator when forced or when DOM is unusable (canvas, remote desktop, captcha, sparse text). Safe default is dry_run.

instruction.description: Browser task to perform or plan.

force_visual.description: Skip DOM strategy and use visual browser operation immediately.

dry_run.description: For visual fallback: parse/plan without moving mouse/keyboard.

max_loop.description: For visual fallback: maximum observe/VLM/action iterations.

loop_wait.description: For visual fallback: seconds between real actions.

function.name: forum_harvest
function.description: Crawl the user's logged-in linux.do session for free-API posts via Discourse JSON (latest.json + /t/<id>.json). Extracts (base_url, key, model) triples and writes them to the candidate queue. Does not call the harvested APIs — pair with api_probe to actually validate. The harvester reuses the existing tmwd_cdp_bridge so all login state / 2FA / Cloudflare cookies stay in the user's real browser.

max_topics.description: Cap on topics fetched per run (default 20). Each topic is one /t/<id>.json fetch.

require_keywords.description: Only scan topics whose title/tags hint at API content (default true). Set false to scan everything.

auto_probe.description: Immediately probe each new candidate after harvesting. Off by default — probing is its own permission prompt.

function.name: api_probe
function.description: Validate a free-pool API endpoint by running the fingerprint question bank. Writes results (scores, latency, actual_model_guess, supported_models) back to the vault. Use action=`probe_one` for an ad-hoc URL/key, `probe_candidates` to drain the candidate queue into the vault, `sweep` to expire+archive stale entries, or `list` to dump the current vault.

base_url.description: probe_one: API base URL ending in /v1 or /api/v1.

key.description: probe_one: bearer key for the endpoint (sk-...).

claimed_model.description: probe_one: model id the poster claimed (used as the candidate's claimed_model).

entry_id.description: archive: which vault entry id to evict.

reason.description: archive: why (recorded into the archive log).

limit.description: probe_candidates: cap on candidates probed this run.

function.name: free_pool_ask
function.description: Single-turn LLM inference through the free pool. Respects the sensitivity gate: only public prompts touch the pool; internal/private are refused or routed elsewhere. Returns the answer plus which entry served it. If the pool is exhausted, returns error=`free_pool_exhausted_no_fallback` (when fallback_to_paid is false) or `free_pool_exhausted_retry_with_main_llm` (when true) — in the second case the caller should re-ask without this tool.

sensitivity.description: Privacy classification. autonomous self-selected tasks must use `public`.

fallback_to_paid.description: Hint to the caller: when free pool exhausts, retry with the main LLM (the tool itself doesn't switch backends).

max_attempts.description: Max free-pool entries to try before giving up.

max_tokens.description: max_tokens for the underlying chat completion.

category_required.description: Only use entries that scored ≥0.7 on this category tag (e.g. `code`, `long_context`).

min_score.description: Lower bound on entry's weighted_average to be considered.

function.name: pm_friction_scan
function.description: PM Track A: scan recent activity logs for friction signals (retry bursts, error-retry pairs, long turns, bad exits), cluster by (signal_type, tool), apply the ≥3 distinct runs provenance gate, and return structured JSON. The tool DOES NOT call an LLM and DOES NOT write proposals — the agent reasons about the returned clusters in its own turn and writes proposals to temp/pm_proposals.md via file_patch/file_write. Also checks the cadence/accept-rate throttle before returning data.

days_window.description: Look back N days of activity logs.

min_distinct_runs.description: Provenance gate: drop clusters supported by fewer than N distinct runs.

force.description: Bypass the cadence/throttle check (use only when the user explicitly asks for an ad-hoc scan).

function.name: pm_proposal_decide
function.description: Record a decision on a PM proposal so the accept-rate tracker updates. Use status='accepted' when the user approves a proposal (it then becomes a TODO/work item), 'rejected' to mark it as not worth doing, or 'deferred' to push the decision later. Deferred decisions do not affect the accept rate.

function.name: mixture_of_agents
function.description: Fan a single prompt out to N model configs in parallel, then synthesise via an aggregator. Different from `MixinSession` (failover) — this runs every member and combines. Use when quality matters more than latency, or to get a multi-model second-opinion. Member names refer to entries in api_configs. Returns the aggregated answer plus per-member outputs and timings. Defaults the aggregator to the first member if not specified.

prompt.description: User question / instruction sent to every member.

member_names.description: Config names from api_configs. Min 1. Run in parallel.

aggregator_name.description: Config that synthesises member answers. Defaults to member_names[0].

function.name: voice
function.description: Audio I/O via OpenAI-compatible /audio endpoints. Actions: (1) `transcribe` — speech-to-text from an audio file; (2) `tts` — text-to-speech, writes binary to `output_path`; (3) `tts_edge` — free local TTS via the optional `edge-tts` package. Picks the first config in mykey with `audio_capable: True` (or known audio-host hints). Returns the transcribed text or output path; `'Error: ...'` on failure.

text.description: Required for tts/tts_edge. The text to synthesise.

output_path.description: Required for tts/tts_edge. Where to write the audio file.

voice.description: TTS voice (e.g. 'alloy' for OpenAI, 'zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural' for edge-tts).

function.name: image_generate
function.description: Generate one or more images from a text prompt via /images/generations. Picks the first mykey config with `image_capable: True` (or known image-host hints). Writes the result to `output_path`; if `n>1` writes numbered siblings (`foo.png`, `foo-2.png`, ...). Returns the primary path or `'Error: ...'`.

output_path.description: Where to write the primary image (e.g. 'temp/img/scene.png').

function.name: skill_propose_patch
function.description: Propose an improvement to an SOP/skill file you just used. The proposal is queued for user review (does NOT modify the file directly). Use after running a skill if you noticed: a missing precondition, an outdated tool name, a clearer phrasing, a new edge case worth documenting. The user can accept (applies + auto-backs-up the original) or reject. Diff format: unified diff (preferred) OR a complete replacement file.

skill_id.description: SOP filename, e.g. 'plan' / 'plan_sop' / 'plan_sop.md'. Looked up in memory/.

diff.description: Unified diff (`---`/`+++`/`@@`) or a complete new file body.

reason.description: Why this change improves the skill.
